description: Zero Trust - Security paradigm operating under the core assumption of 'never trust, always verify'.
Zero Trust Architecture - Enterprise cybersecurity plan enforcing strict identity and microsegmentation controls.
Zero Trust Network Access - Framework providing secure application access based on verified identity and posture.
Policy Enforcement Point - Gatekeeper component in Zero Trust enforcing PDP decisions on network connections.
Policy Decision Point - Zero Trust engine evaluating credentials and posture to decide whether to allow access.
Secure Access Service Edge - Architecture integrating software-defined networking (SD-WAN) with cloud security.
Cloud Access Security Broker - Security gateway managing policies and data encryption between users and cloud services.
Secure Web Gateway - Gateway filtering malicious web traffic and enforcing company internet usage policy.
Web Application Firewall - Layer 7 firewall protecting web applications against SQLi, XSS, and HTTP exploits.
Firewall - Network hardware/software device controlling incoming and outgoing traffic via rule sets.
Next-Generation Firewall - Advanced firewall combining packet inspection with inline IPS and deep application control.
Unified Threat Management - All-in-one security device providing firewalling, IPS, anti-malware, and web filtering.
Intrusion Detection System - Passive security system monitoring network traffic and raising alerts on malicious behavior.
Intrusion Prevention System - Active inline security appliance monitoring traffic and actively blocking detected threats.
Network Intrusion Detection System - IDS dedicated to sniffing and analyzing malicious traffic across entire subnets.
Network Intrusion Prevention System - Inline IPS protecting an entire network segment by actively dropping bad packets.
Host-Based Intrusion Detection System - Agent installed on a single endpoint monitoring system log files and integrity.
Host-Based Intrusion Prevention System - Endpoint security agent actively blocking rogue processes and system unauthorized actions.
Network Access Control - Solution checking endpoint health and security compliance before granting network access.
Data Loss Prevention - Software tools protecting sensitive or confidential data from unauthorized exfiltration.
Digital Rights Management - Access-control technologies limiting the copying, editing, and distribution of proprietary content.
Hardware Security Module - Physical security appliance dedicated to generating, storing, and protecting cryptographic keys.
Trusted Platform Module - Dedicated cryptoprocessor installed on a computer motherboard providing hardware root of trust.
